items.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.summary: The article examines how foundation models, pretrained on natural images, are adapted for medical image segmentation and compares them to task-specific training.
items.whyItMatters: It highlights gaps in evidence for foundation models’ real-world performance, guiding tech-savvy readers on reliable AI deployment.

items.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
items.summary: The article discusses using example-based grounding in EM-DETR to create foundation detection models for medical lesion detection amid limited annotated data.
items.whyItMatters: It could improve diagnostic AI accuracy with fewer costly annotations, benefiting clinicians and patients.

items.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
items.summary: TorchCurves is a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives, enabling differentiation through inputs and coefficients.
items.whyItMatters: It lets tech-savvy readers embed differentiable curve modeling directly into neural networks for advanced geometry tasks.

items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.summary: AutoScaffold uses AI to generate training-time scaffolds that convert detailed RL rewards into actionable guidance for language model learning.
items.whyItMatters: It automates scaffold design, improving RL efficiency and reducing human effort in training large language models.

items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.summary: The paper introduces Contrastive Discovery, a method for LLM agents to evaluate competing scientific hypotheses, not just a single hypothesis versus its negation.
items.whyItMatters: It enables more precise scientific reasoning, helping tech-savvy readers build smarter, evidence‑driven AI discovery tools.

items.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.summary: Pyrite presents a benchmark of 1,500 protein‑ligand pose pairs to evaluate pairwise ranking methods for drug‑binding predictions.
items.whyItMatters: It helps developers assess and improve AI models for more accurate ligand pose ranking in drug discovery.

items.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
items.summary: The article critiques connectome-constrained models, showing they may overstate wiring’s role by conflating structure with tuned parameters like excitability and plasticity.
items.whyItMatters: It warns that claimed structure-function links might be misleading, urging careful model validation for neuroscientists.

items.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.summary: The paper introduces Continual-ARC, a benchmark for measuring skill acquisition over a lifetime, addressing gaps in existing continual learning tests.
items.whyItMatters: It enables fair comparison of memory- and weight-based systems, guiding research toward more robust lifelong learning models.

items.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
items.summary: Bonbon, a foundation model trained on 3.2 trillion protein‑ligand tokens, shows zero‑shot emergent capabilities for molecular interaction tasks.
items.whyItMatters: It could accelerate drug discovery by predicting interactions without task‑specific training.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.summary: The article compares three evaluation frameworks for detecting failures in enterprise LLM analytics agents across complex workflows.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers need reliable failure detection to ensure robust AI deployments in business environments.

items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.summary: ReTrace transforms natural-language SOPs and logged LLM agent runs into reusable code workflows, reducing per-step LLM calls and cutting latency and cost.
items.whyItMatters: It speeds up and economizes large-scale automation for tech teams.

items.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
items.summary: TimeSeek introduces a multi-task, multi-domain pretraining framework to enhance time series models beyond large Transformer stacks, improving adaptability across domains.
items.whyItMatters: It offers more flexible, efficient models for diverse time‑series applications, appealing to developers seeking better performance without massive parameter growth.

items.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
items.summary: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. items.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference
items.summary: Neural networks are increasingly studied not merely as predictive systems, but as complex systems whose internal computations are themselves objects of scientific inquiry. Recent progress in mechanistic interpretability (MI) has made it possible to identify neurons, features, circuits, population structures, and dynamical patterns associated with model behavior. items.title: Pterodactyl: Pushing the Limits of Efficient Automated Translation Evaluation
items.summary: In this paper, we present 1020 Group's submission to the WMT26 shared task on automated quality evaluation. Our system, Pterodactyl, was engineered specifically for subtasks 2 and 3, that is, segment-level quality score prediction and the detection of error-free segments. Pterodactyl is a highly customizable, ultra-low cost system optimized for binary classification in translation triage and data…

items.title: FERN: Cross-Benchmark Table Retrieval for Text-to-SQL with Frozen Retrievers and Learned Ranking
items.summary: Text-to-SQL systems over large pooled catalogs must first retrieve the tables a question needs. We compare against the published table recall of RASL, which uses Claude 3.5 models to extract keywords and select tables, on pooled BIRD, Spider, and Fiben catalogs. items.title: C^2-Routing: Complementary Cropping and Compression for Efficient Vision-Language Inference
items.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) imposes substantial computational overhead on vision-language models (VLMs), motivating model-agnostic input reduction methods that can be readily applied across diverse VLMs, including in black-box settings. items.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
items.summary: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. items.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
items.summary: Policy optimization is central to language model post-training, yet principled guidance remains limited. We revisit its theoretical foundations to identify algorithms that learn near-optimal policies using total samples and gradient steps governed by the base model's response coverage, a measure of how readily it generates optimal responses. items.title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance
items.summary: Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second.
